Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Renewables Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants using speaker equipment are advised that the operator will provide instructions on how to queue up for questions. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Renewables' results for the third quarter. Joining me on today's call are David Morrow, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Michael Torres, Chief Development Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Lisa Grant, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to David Morrow.

David Morrow:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong third quarter performance, driven by our continued focus on innovation, operational excellence, and sustainability. We are seeing strong demand for our renewable energy solutions across all markets.

Here are six key highlights from the quarter:

1. We achieved record revenue of $1.45 billion, up 52% year-over-year and 18% quarter-over-quarter, powered by a 68% surge in our EPC segment to $980 million, with 2.8 GWac of utility-scale solar deployed, including the flagship 1.2 GW Desert Bloom project now exceeding nameplate capacity.

2. Our BESS segment delivered $320 million in revenue, up 110% year-over-year, with 1.5 GWh deployed at expanded 28% gross margins, highlighted by the 850 MWh IronPeak system in ERCOT boasting 92% round-trip efficiency.

3. EBITDA reached $285 million at 19.7% margins, up 320 basis points, bolstered by $145 million in IRA tax credits, while adjusted EPS hit $0.92, beating consensus by 14%, with cumulative installed capacity surpassing 25 GW globally.

4. Our contracted backlog grew to 8.2 GW at an average $32 per MWh PPA price, up 4% quarter-over-quarter, with 1.1 GW in extensions adding $2.8 billion in value at blended $34 per MWh rates.

5. The project pipeline expanded to 45 GW, valued at $28 billion and up 35% year-over-year, with 65% contracted via 15-year PPAs, and key wins like a 10 GW supply deal with NextEra and full permitting for the 1 GW Collie Green H2 project.

6. We gained 250 basis points of U.S. market share to 12%, driven by faster NTP timelines, domestic content at 85%, and ESG leadership with Scope 1&2 emissions down 40% year-over-year.

Now, I will turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, David. We are very pleased with our financial performance in the third quarter. Revenue was $1.45 billion, a 52% increase year-over-year. This increase was driven by higher project commissioning and energy sales. Gross margin was 28%, reflecting improved cost management and favorable pricing. Operating expenses were $156 million, primarily due to increased investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $180 million, or $0.92 per share. We ended the quarter with $1.1 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings, now raised to $5.4-$5.5 billion in revenue and $1.18-$1.22 adjusted EPS.

Let me expand on some critical financial drivers starting with PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, which remain a cornerstone of our revenue stability and long-term growth. PPAs are the lifeblood of our 12 GW portfolio of solar, wind, and hybrid assets across North America, Europe, and select APAC markets. Our Q3 contracted backlog stood at 8.2 GW with an average remaining life of 11.2 years and a weighted average PPA price of $32 per MWh, up 4% quarter-over-quarter from strategic repricing and extensions.

On pricing trends, the market shows resilience despite moderating costs. In the US, 65% of our PPA revenue, solar prices stabilized at $22-26/MWh for utility-scale in ERCOT and MISO auctions, down from 2022 peaks due to a 25% YoY LCOE drop to $18-22/MWh per NREL. Module prices hit $0.22/Wp for TOPCon bifacial from JinkoSolar and Trina, with trackers down 15% via Nextracker. Yet in CAISO, our 1.8 GW contracts cleared RFPs at $28-32/MWh for solar-plus-storage hybrids using Tesla Megapacks and Fluence Gridstack, commanding 20-30% premiums. Wind in SPP and PJM signed at $25-30/MWh, leveraging IRA PTC extensions for our 2.1 GW fleet.

In Europe, post-energy crisis, unsubsidized PPAs reached €35-45/MWh per LevelTen, up 10% YoY, with our 850 MW extended at €42/MWh amid REPowerEU. APAC softened to AUD 45-55/MWh in Australia, but our 300 MW Queensland deals held at AUD 52/MWh. Tailwinds include 12% YoY EPC cost drops, stabilized steel and copper, and our $1.2B green bond at 4.8%.

On extensions, we closed 1.1 GW in Q3, adding $2.8B at $34/MWh, 15% above expiring rates. Highlights include a 500 MW Texas wind repower from Vestas V90 to higher-yield tech, and a California solar extension with 100 MW/400 MWh BESS at $45/MWh shaped PPA. US drove 70%, Europe 25% via corporate deals like Shell's Dutch offshore with Siemens Gamesa 14 MW turbines. We've blended VPPA for 20% of offtake with Google and Amazon, diversifying buyers: utilities 55%, hyperscalers 25%, industrials 20%.

Forward, we target $5-7B in new PPAs/extensions at $30-35/MWh, using AI optimization with Stem Inc. for 8% price uplift, and green H2 pilots at €60/MWh equivalent. Risks like PJM queues are mitigated by 90% contracted utilization.

Next, on capital expenditures and operating expenses. CAPEX totaled $428 million, up 22% QoQ and 45% YoY, aligned with 2.5 GW pipeline activation. Solar PV took 58% or $248 million for 750 MWdc projects like SunForge in ERCOT at $0.92/Wdc EPC, aided by IRA domestic content. BESS 28% or $120 million for 400 MWh LFP at $185/kWh from CATL/BYD. Wind 9% or $39 million for Vestas V150, and 5% for grid upgrades. North America 72%, Europe 18%, APAC 10%. Efficiency hit $1.05M/MWac, FY24 guide $1.6-1.8B.

OPEX at $156 million, 24% of revenue, flat as % YoY. O&M 42% or $65M at $12/kWac/year, with drones cutting solar downtime 18%; wind $35/kW fixed. SG&A $42M up 12% on hiring, offset by RPA. R&D/G&A $49M for perovskites and VPP. OPEX intensity down 7% to $22/kWac. FY margins to expand to 35% by 2026.

Regarding debt levels and financing costs, total gross debt was $5.2 billion, down from $5.4B YE23, with net debt $4.1B after $1.1B cash. Debt/EBITDA at 3.5x, targeting <4.0x. Project leverage 70-80% construction, 45% stabilized. Interest expense $218M or 4.2% cost, down 110 bps YoY from fixed-rate locks, $1B green bonds at 3.8%, and sustainability loans. US tax equity, Europe EIB, APAC samurai bonds. Maturity 7.2 years average, deleveraging via $800M rotations. FY interest $850-900M, cost to 4.0%.

Finally, tax equity and project-level financing. We closed $1.2B tax equity in Q3, YTD $2.8B or 65% of needs, via flips like $650M for Gemini Solar+Storage at 8.5% IRR target. Transferability sold $180M ITCs at 95% NPV. ERCOT compressed to 6.8%, PJM 9.2%. Project debt $3.4B at SOFR+175bps for 1.8 GW, storage hybrids boosting DSCR to 1.8x. Diversified 12 investors, portfolio financings at 5.5%. Pipeline needs $15-18B over 24 months.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Torres for an update on our project pipeline.

Michael Torres:
Thank you, Sarah. Our project pipeline continues to grow, with 45 GW under development per S&P Global rankings, positioning us as the #3 U.S. developer. Valued at $28 billion, up 35% YoY, with 65% contracted at $35/MWh blended over 15 years. We're advancing on land rights, permits, and PPAs, expecting several GW online soon. Highlights include 2.5 GW U.S. solar RECs, 800 MWac Spain hybrids, 400 MW Indonesia floating solar, and 1 GW Rajasthan PPA. We're pursuing acquisitions and partnerships like Fortescue for green H2, with $7.2B backlog spanning EPC/IPP/O&M. U.S. 60%, Europe 25%, APAC/LatAm rest.

Next, Elena Vasquez will provide an update on our technology initiatives.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Michael. We are committed to developing and deploying innovative technologies that improve the efficiency and reliability of renewable energy systems. Significant progress includes perovskite-silicon tandem modules at 29.8% NREL-tested efficiency from our 5 GW Texas Gigafactory, securing 10 GW NextEra supply. Storage vertical integration cut costs 22% to $145/kWh for IronPeak's 92% RTE. Green H2 electrolyzer at 75% efficiency producing $2.10/kg in Rotterdam, de-risking 1 GW Collie. AuroraFlow AI EMS reduces inefficiencies 15%, VFBs for long-duration, and HDPE floaters for typhoon resilience. The development of our next-gen perovskite tandem solar is expected to boost project IRRs by 200 bps and enable 30%+ efficiencies, transforming future hybrids.

And now, Lisa Grant will provide an update on our sustainability efforts.

Lisa Grant:
Thank you, Elena. We are committed to operating our business in a sustainable manner and minimizing our environmental impact. We've set ambitious goals for reducing carbon emissions 40% YoY in Scope 1&2 via 100% renewable factories, earning S&P CSA 85/100. Energy efficiency improvements, responsible resource management with biodiversity offsets, and $15M in community training for 5,000 jobs in solar hubs. 92% contracted utilization, domestic content 85%, and SBTi net-zero by 2030 make sustainability core to value creation.

I'll now turn the call back to David Morrow for closing remarks.

David Morrow:
Thank you, Lisa. In closing, we are confident that Apex Renewables is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for renewable energy. To outline our strategic priorities and outlook, the sector enjoys $1.8T global investments, solar LCOE under $25/MWh, policy like IRA/REPowerEU. Priorities: 1) U.S. manufacturing ramp—5 GW module fab Q2 2025, 2 GWh LFP Arizona with $450M credits for 20% backlog supply. 2) R&D to 8% revenue for perovskites 30%+, VFBs, H2 under $2/kg. 3) Backlog monetization—$7.2B, 1.8 GW U.S. construction, offshore Europe, India/Brazil. 4) Supply chain—50k tons polysilicon offtake, ESG net-zero 2030. 5) M&A $500-800M, Siemens MOU.

Q4 revenue $1.6-1.7B, FY24 $5.4-5.5B up 48%, EBITDA $850-875M. FY25 $6.2-6.5B revenue, 30% growth. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Operator, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question at this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. We'll pause for a moment to assemble the queue. Our first question comes from Emily Carter with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
Can you provide more details on the regulatory environment for renewable energy projects in your key markets?

David Morrow:
Thanks, Emily. The regulatory landscape is supportive overall. In the U.S., IRA extensions drive ITC/PTC monetization and manufacturing credits, shielding from tariffs while RPS mandates boost REC premiums. FERC Order 2222 aids distributed resources, though PJM queues average 4-5 years—we're #14 for 2 GW. Europe's REPowerEU mandates 600 GW by 2030, with €270B funds aiding Spain/Poland despite grid codes. APAC leverages Australia's Clean H2 Mission and India's NTPC bids, but permitting varies. We've localized 85% domestic content to maximize adders, and policy risks like IRA tweaks are hedged by 90% contracted backlog.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly:
How is the company addressing the challenges of energy storage integration with your renewable energy projects?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Tom. Storage integration is pivotal for firming renewables. We've deployed 1.5 GWh in Q3, shifting to LFP for cost/degradation advantages, achieving $145-185/kWh with 92% RTE. Hybrids like CAISO solar+BESS command 20-30% PPA uplifts, arbitraging duck curves via AuroraFlow AI EMS, cutting dispatch losses 15%. IronPeak's 850 MWh standalone and VFB pilots offer 20-year cycles. Partnerships with Tesla/Fluence, vertical integration, and IRA bonuses ensure bankability, with 70% fleet LFP targeting LCOS under $35/MWh.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen:
What are your expectations for the long-term growth of the renewable energy market?

David Morrow:
Laura, we're bullish long-term. IEA sees renewables at 50% of global additions by 2025, BNEF $150B IPP auctions to 2030. Solar/wind LCOE beats gas, electrification from EVs/AI/data centers drives demand. Our 45 GW pipeline, 15 GW capacity target by 2027, and tech edge position us for 25-30% CAGR. Policy tailwinds, supply deflation to $0.22/W modules, and hyperscaler PPAs fuel this, with risks like queues offset by diversification.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to David Morrow for any closing remarks.

David Morrow:
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Renewables. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
